Sophie —

Appreciate the summary and the doc. Looping in Marissa (contracts lead) and Karthik (security/compliance) to own the redlines and the transfer impact. High level from our side:

- Redwood will offer SCCs for EU transfers and can execute the UK IDTA addendum where required.
- We surface subprocessors in the DPA and maintain a 30-day notice for new ones; for any subprocessor that triggers a cross-border transfer we add the transfer impact statement.
- We prefer DocuSign for most enterprise signings (faster for OrbitPay?) but can send a PDF for AdobeSign if you require it.

Targeting: Marissa will send our initial redline by EOD today (12 May). Once you confirm a signature platform, we will bundle the DPA + UK addendum in a single envelope and route to your legal and procurement contacts.

Hi Sophie —

Attached are our proposed redlines (OrbitPay_DPA_redlines_20270512.pdf). Key callouts:

1) UK IDTA addendum: we accept the standard addendum with a limited-scope deviation that clarifies routing of incident notifications to your UK security lead and adds a specific audit window (30 days notice).
2) Transfer impact statement: we propose a short annex that enumerates jurisdictions, the legal basis (SCCs), and a mitigation paragraph referencing our technical controls (encryption in transit at rest, limited cross-border subprocessors).
3) Subprocessors: we will list current subprocessors in the exhibit and commit to 30-day notice for changes; critical subprocessors will be routed through the same SCCs.
4) E-sign flow: recommend DocuSign single-envelope with: OrbitPay signers -> Redwood counter-sign (marissa@redwood.ai) -> final legal copy to both parties. If OrbitPay needs AdobeSign, we can produce a PDF bundle and route manually.

Please review the attached redlines and confirm any material concerns. If you’re good, I’ll prepare the DocuSign envelope and request signatures Friday.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference
